title: The Animals Become Helpers
subtitle: Each prince spares a mother animal

helpers.excerpt: The eldest Prince was about to shoot at her, but the bear cried out, “Do not shoot, Prince, and I will give you my three cubs for servants, one for you, and one for each of your brothers.” To this the Prince agreed. He let the bear go away unharmed, and the three cubs followed after the three Princes, each one behind his own master. After they had gone a bit farther into the forest, they saw a lioness, and she also had three young ones with her. Now it was the second Prince who was about to shoot, but the lioness called to him, “Do not slay me, Prince, and I will give my three cubs to you and your brothers, one to each of you.” Thereupon the Prince allowed her to go unharmed and the three young lions followed after the Princes with the bear cubs. Soon after that they saw a mother fox, and three little ones were with her. This time it was the youngest Prince who would have shot, but the fox called to him, imploring him to spare her life and offering instead her three young ones to the Princes. She too was allowed to escape, and now each Prince had a young fox, a young lion and a young bear to follow him.
helpers.note: Verbatim text from Katherine Pyle's 1922 English children's retelling. The collection labels it Lithuanian but does not identify an oral informant or underlying source text.

narrativeBlocks.title: A bear asks to be spared
narrativeBlocks.body: When the princes meet a mother bear and her cubs, she asks them not to kill her and offers one cub to each brother.

narrativeBlocks.title: Lioness and fox follow
narrativeBlocks.body: The second prince spares a lioness, then the youngest spares a fox. By the end, each prince is followed by a bear, lion, and fox cub.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not universalize animal meanings
narrativeBlocks.body: The tale gives these animals specific roles in Pyle's retelling. It does not establish a fixed Baltic symbolism for bears, lions, or foxes.

narrativeBlocks.title: The helpers follow acts of mercy
narrativeBlocks.body: The princes gain companions after sparing each mother animal in this story's sequence.
